questions.definition: The smallest particle of an element that can take part in chemical reactions.
questions.explanation: Atoms have a nucleus containing protons and neutrons, with electrons arranged in shells around the nucleus.

questions.definition: A substance made of only one type of atom.
questions.explanation: Elements cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

questions.definition: A substance made from two or more elements chemically bonded together.
questions.explanation: Compounds have fixed ratios of elements and properties that are different from the elements they contain.

questions.definition: Two or more substances together that are not chemically bonded.
questions.explanation: Mixtures can be separated using methods such as filtration, distillation, chromatography, or crystallisation.

questions.definition: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
questions.clue: Same proton number, different mass number.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons.

questions.definition: A strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
questions.clue: Often forms between metals and non-metals.
questions.explanation: Ionic bonding happens when electrons are transferred and ions form a giant lattice structure.

questions.definition: A bond formed when atoms share pairs of electrons.
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding allows atoms to achieve more stable outer electron shells by sharing electrons.

questions.definition: The decomposition of an ionic compound using electricity.
questions.clue: Requires a molten or aqueous electrolyte.
questions.explanation: During electrolysis, ions move to electrodes where they gain or lose electrons.

questions.definition: A reaction where a substance gains oxygen or loses electrons.
questions.explanation: In redox reactions, oxidation and reduction happen together. Electron loss is oxidation.

questions.definition: A reaction where a substance loses oxygen or gains electrons.
questions.explanation: Reduction is important in extracting metals from their ores, such as removing oxygen from metal oxides.

questions.definition: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up.
questions.explanation: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy and can be reused.

questions.definition: A separation technique used to separate substances in a mixture based on their movement through a medium.
questions.clue: Often used with inks or dyes.
questions.explanation: Different substances move different distances depending on their solubility and attraction to the stationary phase.
